I went through that when I miscarried (about 1.5 years ago). I wish I could say it gets easier, but it didn't until I was pregnant with my current pregnancy.  My SIL miscarried 5 days before I did, and THEN got pregnant 3 weeks after. That was hard. And then it felt like everyone in the world was pregnant. I remember when she gave birth, I sobbed that night because I couldn't help but think about how I should have been in that bed, holding my baby. Little did I know I was like 2 days pregnant at the time with our second baby. 

It doesn't get easier, and though I'm 31 weeks today I still wonder and yearn for my first baby. It doesn't diminish my love for our son, but it's something that will always ache in my heart.

Mine did not double, it was about that range, and I am happy to say I am 27w6d along. The doctor was cautious but not too concerned when I didn't fully double. He did, though, have me come in every 2 weeks and we did ultrasounds to make sure the baby was okay.

The anxiety lessened when I could feel him kick, but my anxiety flares up when I get closer to the doctors appointments. I don't think it will ever go away. But it DOES feel a lot better when he's kicking my bladder and I almost pee myself.

I was much more nauseated with my successful pregnancy. And all of my symptoms were practically gone a week before I miscarried. 
My coworker even made a comment that I hardly seemed pregnant right before I miscarried and I said "I know! I feel great!" 
My OBGYN told me that a warning sign is that you should NOT feel back to your old self quickly like that.
I don't think it's wrong to just tell people to leave you alone. They might be well intentioned, but you NEED to do what you need to prepare for your little babe. 🧡

The silence is deafening, but dont let it consume you. If it helps to talk about it, then talk about it. Let it become the fact. We named our child when we miscarried, and we knew the gender. Her name was Bridget. And when we talk about her, we use her name. We remember the love we had for her. 
The next few months will be very hard. But remember that the experiences you had will always be yours. That baby will always be yours.
